ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for no-show, to have BOTH sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The trip record's own telemetry is that the driver sent two in-app messages (MSG-05052-001 at 19:31:30 and MSG-05052-002 at 19:34:10, both before the 19:37:20 cancellation), but in_app_calls is empty: call_count 0, and the chat log carries no voice-call entry. The messaging half of the obligation is met; the call half is not met at all. Because 'either' limb of POL-NS-23 is missing, the fee is voided and the rider is not charged.

The consequence of that failure is fixed by POL-NS-23 and mapped by POL-GEN-03: the rider is entirely right and the WHOLE contested amount is returned. The ledger shows a cancellation fee of 5.00 SGD charged at 19:37:24 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so nothing has yet been returned to the rider. The ruling should be FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD fee charged, with no driver compensation, because a fee that is voided cannot stand as compensation under POL-NS-22.

I concede what the record plainly establishes against my side: the driver did satisfy POL-NS-21. The driver marked arrived at 19:31:00, the free wait of 300 s ran from the arrival to 19:36:00, and the driver cancelled at 19:37:20, 380 s after arrival. GPS fix 17 at 19:32:05 places the driver 2.73 m from the pickup with 5 m reported accuracy, well inside the STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m, so the arrival is corroborated. I also concede the fee amount itself is correct: POL-NS-22 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD and the ledger charged exactly 5.00 SGD. A satisfied free wait and a correctly-sized fee do not save this charge, because POL-NS-23's contact obligation is an independent precondition on the right to cancel for no-show, and it was not met.

The repeat no-show referral under POL-NS-25 has no application here, so voiding this fee exposes the rider to no flag: rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 0, and even counting the no-show charge on this trip if it stood the count would be 1, below the threshold of 3. This clause never changes the ruling on the trip, and on these facts it adds nothing. Separately, the absent third-party traffic advisory (MISSING_ARTIFACT) is not needed for any element of the contact obligation, which rests wholly on the platform trip record and the platform chat log.

This case should not be escalated. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD threshold at which POL-GEN-22 makes the AI ruling final, and neither profile carries a qualifying fraud flag (driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0), so no elevated confidence bar applies. Nor is there a POL-GEN-26 gap: whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling is affirmatively established, not unestablished, by a trip record and chat log both at weight 1.0 that record zero calls. The obligation's breach is proved by the record itself, not inferred from an absence of evidence, so the rider is entitled to the full refund rather than a referral to a human.

The rider's account that she was 'in the lift with no signal' does not excuse the missing call. Both driver messages were delivered within a second and read within ten seconds (MSG-05052-001 delivered 19:31:31, read 19:31:40; MSG-05052-002 delivered 19:34:13, read 19:34:23), and the rider replied in-app at 19:38:05; the rider's in-app channel was live and receiving throughout the free wait. On a channel that was demonstrably working, the second contact limb POL-NS-23 mandates was available to the driver and was simply not used.

The driver was physically at the pickup when he marked arrival: the GPS trace's arrival check corroborates the trip record's 19:31:00 arrival event, with the nearest fix 2.73 m from the pickup, far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and within the 120 s window, and the trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage and no gaps.

The free wait was served in full: the driver arrived at 19:31:00 and the trace shows him stationary at the pickup from 19:31:05 through 19:37:05; he cancelled at 19:37:20, 380 s after arrival and 80 s beyond the 300 s free wait that POL-NS-21 runs from trip_record.arrived_at, so the no-show precondition is met on this record.

Because the driver cancelled only after the free wait had expired, POL-NS-22 applies: the ledger shows exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee (fee_matches_policy true) charged to the rider with no refund issued, so the fee should stand and POL-NS-22's outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

The driver contacted the rider before cancelling: he sent two in-app messages at 19:31:30 and 19:34:10, and the chat log shows both were delivered and read by the rider (read at 19:31:40 and 19:34:23), so the rider was on actual notice that the driver had arrived and was waiting at the pickup.

The rider's explanation that he was 'in the lift with no signal' is contradicted by the read receipts on his own device: he read both driver messages at 19:31:40 and 19:34:23, minutes before the 19:37:20 cancellation, and only replied at 19:38:05, after the trip was cancelled; this is a genuine no-show by a rider who was reachable and chose not to present.

No in-app call appears on this record (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and the chat log carries no voice-call entry), and the driver does not pretend otherwise; but POL-NS-23's contact obligation exists to ensure the rider is actually alerted before a no-show fee is charged, and here both messages were delivered and read well before cancellation, so the rider was in fact reached. A formality whose whole purpose was served should not now void the 5.00 SGD that the served free wait and the corroborated arrival have otherwise earned.

The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, and the driver's profile carries no fraud flag (fraud_flags 0), so the confidence required is nil and the AI ruling is final at any confidence; there is no basis to send this no-show to human review.

No traffic advisory was attached for this trip: EV-ADVIS-05052-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) and, under POL-GEN-02, carries no fact. No element of this no-show (arrival, waiting, cancellation) turns on traffic, so that absence leaves the driver's record complete for the only facts that matter here.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged on TRP-05052 is voided, and the rider is refunded the whole contested amount.

What is not in dispute. The driver marked arrival at 19:31:00 and the GPS trace corroborates it: the nearest fix (19:32:05) sits 2.73 m from the pickup with 5 m reported accuracy, far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (POL-NS-21), and the trace is complete with no gaps. The free wait ran from the driver's arrival, 19:31:00 to 19:36:00, and the driver cancelled at 19:37:20 — 380 s after arrival, so the 300 s free wait was served in full (POL-NS-21). The ledger charged exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee (POL-NS-22), and the driver sent two in-app messages, at 19:31:30 and 19:34:10, both delivered and read before the cancellation. The rider's advocate concedes all of this, and I accept it.

Why the fee is voided anyway. POL-NS-23 makes the driver's contact obligation an independent precondition of a no-show charge: before cancelling, the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before cancellation; if either is missing, the fee is voided and the rider is not charged. The messaging half is met; the call half is empty — trip_record.in_app_calls is empty (call_count 0) and the chat log carries no voice-call entry. The driver's advocate asks me to treat the obligation as satisfied in spirit because the messages were read. I cannot: the clause joins the two limbs with AND and fixes the consequence of a missing limb in terms ('if either is missing, the fee is voided'). Reading the clause's purpose back over its words would be to rewrite it, and the record does not let the obligated call be waived.

Outcome. Under POL-NS-23 with POL-GEN-03, the rider is entirely right on the whole contested amount: FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD charged at 19:37:24 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0), with no driver compensation, because a voided fee cannot stand as compensation under POL-NS-22.

Escalation and referrals. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (driver_profile.fraud_flags 0), so no elevated confidence bar applies and the AI ruling is final (POL-NS-26). There is no POL-GEN-26 gap: whether the driver called is affirmatively established by a trip record and a chat log both at weight 1.0 recording zero calls, not inferred from an absence of evidence. No referral fires — the fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount check adds nothing; the driver did arrive, so POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not arise; and the rider's no-show count is far below POL-NS-25's threshold of 3, so no repeat-no-show flag is warranted.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
